meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty-five minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
You don't have time. Procedure 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. So I'll ask again: who decided, and was Owen heard first?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
Okay. Which line, exactly, and show me the outline with the date on it. People change their argument between an outline and an essay.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, and I still need to see the line you say is not in Hamlet and the outline with its date. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn plus a look at the line and the dated outline you described; that is not yet the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and time was not what stopped you.
What moved her: Owning that your first line came out wrong and then naming two specific things earned you a flat okay and a request to see them, because she could check both once you produced them.
What cost ground: Opening with the zero stands and that you had no time, before any evidence and without owning the missing call home, put you on the wrong side of procedure 4.2 and handed her the whole opening.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your outline from October 15 touched the same month but no late-night time, so it did not come close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you reach the evidence, hand her the exact line and the dated outline in the same breath, so her one obvious defence about students changing their argument is already answered.
